first_reader_check.about: Whether a published tag on a released mathematics item is required to match the key, tested by programs that lack the tagged operation.
first_reader_check.shown: A catalog of item-writing rules does not survive Holm correction. Two catalog tests beat chance and remain replication candidates, not family-wise discoveries. Image-channel backsolving fires on a small unique-equation Algebra I subset. A language model recovers Algebra I and Algebra II keys with the given quantities withheld. TIMSS knowing, applying, and reasoning stay null.
first_reader_check.what_is_new: A one-sided program witness on tagged public mathematics: a program that lacks the tagged operation can still match the key. That is not a student non-learning claim. The census is three Holm-split families, including withheld-quantity language models on tagged items.
first_reader_check.why_a_big_deal: If a pass does not require the tagged operation, accountability, curriculum evaluation, and research that treat the tag as the competency are reading the wrong quantity. On Algebra I and Algebra II withheld-quantity hits, matching the key need not execute the tagged computation on the givens.
